transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I'm here because I just... I can't shut my brain off anymore. It starts with just one concern. Like a client not responding to an email. But then, within minutes, I'm... I'm convinced I'll lose the contract, and then I'll fall behind on my divorce payments, and... I don't know, never get back to a real leadership role. It just... it doesn't stop.
Do you experience physical symptoms like a racing heart or trembling when these thoughts overwhelm you?
Um... I haven't really noticed anything like that. I'm not sure. It's mostly just... the thoughts.
Has something very stressful or traumatic happened to you recently?
Um... no. Not really. Nothing traumatic, anyway. Just... the usual work stuff, I guess.
Do you find yourself worrying about lots of different things in your daily life, not just work?

Yeah... I suppose. It... it jumps around a lot. Um... I'll think about the contract work, and then... the mortgage. Or... I don't know, whether people in the Bethesda tech circles think I'm... damaged goods. It just... if a recruiter delays an email, I start thinking my whole career is closing down. So... yes. It's a lot of things.
How long have you been experiencing these overwhelming thoughts and worries?

Um... well... I guess it started back when I lost my job... about thirteen months ago. I was fired. And... it just sort of kept going, even after I picked up the contract stuff. It just... hasn't really stopped.
Have these worries been interfering with your daily life or relationships in a significant way?

Yeah... I suppose. It's... it gets in the way. 

Work-wise, I've... well, I've delayed some client deliverables lately. And missed some networking follow-ups. I just sit there and... get stuck anticipating everything that could go wrong with it. So I put it off. 

And... I guess I don't really see friends much right now, either. I pulled back from my soccer league. I just... I'm so tense and irritable all the time, it's kind of embarrassing to be around people. So I just... keep to myself, mostly.
Would you say that your worries generally revolve around a few central themes, like work or finances, or do they cover a wide range of topics?
Um... I don't know. I guess it's mostly work and... money. But it can be other things too. It just... it's a lot of things.
Do you worry about these things every day?

Yeah... pretty much every day. It's just... always there. 

Like, my mind just keeps jumping around. One minute I'm stressing about the contract work, then I'm thinking about the mortgage payments... and then I start wondering if people in the Bethesda tech circles think I'm just... damaged goods now. It doesn't take much to set it off. Like, if a recruiter delays an email, I just... I start thinking it's proof my whole career is basically over. So, yeah... it's every day.
Do these worries usually start after something specific happens, or can they come out of the blue?

Um... sometimes it's out of nowhere, I guess. But usually it starts with just one concern. Like a client not responding. 

And then I just... I can't shut my brain off anymore. Within a few minutes, I'm already convinced I'm going to lose the contract, and... well, fall behind on my divorce payments. And then I start thinking I'll never get back to a real leadership role. It just... it gets away from me.
When you're worrying, are you usually thinking about things that might happen in the future?
Yeah... mostly the future, I guess. Just... what's coming next.
When these worries start, are you usually able to control them or stop them from escalating?
No... not really. Um... like I just said, I can't shut my brain off. Once it starts with that one little thing, I can't stop it from... you know, getting to all the rest of it. It just takes over.
Have you ever experienced a traumatic event in your life?
No. Nothing like that. Just... normal life stuff, I guess. Nothing traumatic.
Do you feel like you're able to calm down or distract yourself from these worries at all, or do they completely take over?

Not really. They just... take over. That's actually why I finally came in, because I just can't shut my brain off anymore. 

It starts with just one thing. Like a client not responding to an email. And I can't distract myself. Within minutes I'm... I'm convinced I'm going to lose the contract, and then... well, fall behind on my divorce payments. And that I'll never get back to a real leadership role. It just spirals, and... no, I can't calm down once it does.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain situations or activities because of these worries?

Yeah, I guess so. I mean... I've been putting off following up with contacts, networking stuff. And I've been late on some deliverables for clients lately. It's just... I start thinking about all the ways it could go wrong, and I just get stuck. 

And... I don't know, I've kind of stopped going to my soccer games. Haven't been seeing my friends much either. I just... I'm so tense all the time, and I snap at people. It's embarrassing. So it's just easier to stay home.
Are there any areas of your life where you feel you don't worry at all?
Um... no. I don't think so. I can't really think of any... it's pretty much just everywhere, I guess.
Do you think your worries are bigger than the problems themselves?

I guess so. Yeah. It's just... my mind keeps jumping around. 

From contract work... to the mortgage payments. Or I start wondering if people in the Bethesda tech circles think I'm... damaged goods. It gets to the point where just a delayed email from a recruiter can feel like proof that my whole career is closing down. 

So... yeah. I suppose they probably are.
Do you think you worry more than other people about these kinds of things?
I... yeah, probably. I don't really know what goes on in other people's heads, but... it seems like they handle things better. So, yeah. I guess I do.

You mentioned earlier that nothing traumatic has happened to you, but I want to make sure: is there any possibility that these worries started after something upsetting happened, even if it didn't seem traumatic at the time?
I... no. Not really. I mean, nothing stands out. I can't think of anything specific that would have set it off. So... no.
Do you think your worries are interfering with your ability to make decisions or take action in your daily life?

Yeah... I guess you could say that. I've... I've let some things slide. 

Missed some networking follow-ups. Delayed a few client deliverables. I just... I get stuck. I start anticipating every single thing that could go wrong, and I just can't move forward. 

And... I don't know. I've pulled back from other stuff, too. Like soccer, and... seeing friends. I just get so tense and irritable lately. It's embarrassing, honestly. So I just... stay away.
